detail: In pylint/lint/expand_modules.py, _is_in_ignore_list_re does file_pattern.match(element) -- anchored at start only, not fullmatch. _is_ignored_file checks basename against ignore/ignore-patterns, and full element string against ignore-paths. For directories, element=root from os.walk, which is built as something-arg + subdir components, e.g. running 'pylint mypkg' gives roots like mypkg/src/gen, not src/gen. So a pattern like '^src/gen/.*$' only matches if root literally starts with 'src/gen/', which depends on how pylint was invoked (cwd, relative/absolute arg). This is a real footgun for ignore-paths authoring, independent of the missing-per-file-check bug -- confirmed with a small python re test, not a bug in _discover_files control flow itself.

detail: In pylint/checkers/misc.py EncodingChecker.open() (~line 119-128), the fixme regex is built as rf"#\s*({notes})\b" (or with notes_rgx alternative), notes being re.escape'd config.notes joined with |. A note tag entirely punctuation (e.g. "???") never has a \w char adjacent to the match end, so \b never matches even though the literal substring is present — regex search returns None. Alphanumeric tags (YES, FIXME, XXX, TODO) work fine since \b succeeds between the trailing word char and following whitespace/EOL.
